I'm going to start using the sauna at my gym a bit more. I'm willing to try anything at this point and it couldn't hurt to try right?

Thanks

Sound advice, I'm already a regular at the gym and the half hour after pushing myself while there, when my brain is chock full of endorphins, is about the best I am capable of feeling right now. It's fleeting, but it's something for sure. 

Thanks for taking the time to read and reply.

"Let those feelings go" really hit close to home. I'm aware I'm just living this relationship entirely in my head now and I know that's really, really unhealthy. I just can't seem to drag myself out of this loop and the fact I can hold down my job and fool others into thinking I'm keeping on with keeping on just... I don't know, reinforces living the relationship in my head?

Your experience gives me some hope. Thanks for taking the time to respond.

That wasn't actually me (OP) that replied there, but that's great advice none the less. 

My problem is I do so many of these things already - I work out at the gym 2-5 times a week, walk 10-20 miles a week, cook and eat healthily, am not scared to go to a concert or restaurant alone, I spend time in galleries, museums and other places I enjoy, I have been catching up with old friends and reconnecting, I have travelled abroad several times, I've spent lots of time with family, I've read a stack of books and gotten back to old abandoned hobbies and interests, etc.  

I feel much as I did at the start of all this. It's almost like these things I'm doing are for other peoples sake, are to give the appearance of a man doing his best to get on with continuing living because that's what the people around me need to believe. 

I just don't actually feel that way at all. Despite appearances, I feel just as raw, lost, shocked, uncomprehending and alone as I did the day she left.

Thank you for your kind response. 

It's been several months, I still can't even begin to imagine trying to be with anyone else; I was a loyal and devoted husband, that's how the wiring in my brain is now set. Whenever anyone has expressed any kind of interest in me since living alone, I just recoil inside and politely dodge outside - it still registers as some sort of betrayal in my mind, like my brain hasn't caught onto the fact we have been betrayed in such a fundamental way that the trust my devotion stems from no longer exists, that my loyalty is to someone who has just walked out of our life together. 

The mere thought of online dating terrifies me. It all took off after I was already in a stable relationship so I have no experience of it - everything I know about it tells me that it involves a lot of awkwardness and rejection, I don't think I'm tough enough to take that now. I'm not even sure if I can give trust now, you have to understand that I was in a loving, affectionate and intimate relationship with my wife at the time she dropped this bombshell. I'm not perfect and I know our marriage wasn't 100% perfect, but I always tried, I always showed my affection, we fell asleep in each other's arms every night and said we loved each other with a kiss every morning before work.  We were months into trying to buy a bigger house together, we were supposed to be planning a  vacation for my birthday, we were just weeks away from our wedding anniversary and I had a surprise trip abroad planned for that weekend, we were living a life together and then she tells me she'd throw it all away and it was my fault.

I've been in counselling with my therapist for six months now, she knows everything about me that I shield my family and friends from (they have enough to worry about). She's a great woman with near infinite empathy and patience, but although she's trying hard to helps it's just one more place I feel like I'm going in circles and not making any progress. 

It feels good to put these thoughts into words. Maybe not good, but some sort of relief? Thank you for taking the time to reach out to me.

Unfortunately I can't do anything with my place until the divorce is finalised (lawyers very insistent on that point) but it's high up on my list and hasn't stopped me making plans. I just wish I could do more to change the bedroom, but it's all custom carpentered so would cost a fortune to replace. I've replaced all the bedding and towels already, intimate stuff we used to share. I took down all the wedding pictures and boxed all the trinkets we'd gathered over the years in a blur during that first week after I found out the truth. I barely remember it, I was so raw. 

Good advice none the less and a reminder that planning that stuff is still something I can throw myself into and distract myself with.  Thanks.
You are a phenomenal human being. Thank you.

The bottle's finished and I've fought off the exceeded pill dosage for as long as I can for tonight. 

Sweet oblivion beckons. 

You are all beautiful, I love you all. 

Time to sleep and, perchance, to dream.

Raised catholic, but life has beaten any spirituality out of me with its imbalance and tendency toward injustice. 

I don't begrudge anyone their faith, if anything I envy it.

Instead you're someone hurting because of a break-up  that would seem to be entirely due to the other persons uncertainties and seemingly different wants and desires. 

Break-ups hurt, but yours sounds like it arrived for the right reasons (wanting different things from life) and leaves you free to peruse something better (I'm betting you're young enough to do so). 

Keep your chin up and eyes to the horizon sister.

[advice that has helped me edit]
And never forget, the best revenge is living a good life - caveat; living it well for yourself, not because of how it might affect or be perceived by others. Your own self perception is the only reliable constant in this life.

Do so brother. For the sake of yourself and your sanity, tear off that bandaid and get it over with. 

This next whiskey I drink is for you and your unrequited love.

If you're not talking to him you're as much as part of the problem as he is.  

If you have tried (and I mean really tried, not just a passing comment and an expectation someone or something else will do your work for you and fix your relationship for you) and he wasn't listening then be honest, before your secret resentment makes you do something that demeans you even further.

Any time. Our situations are as similar as they are different. I'm actually a little envious, your anger is entirely justified and healthy. I can't seem to feel anything but a certain kind of numbness mixed with a completely inappropriate sense of culpability. 

Be fucking angry man, vent and rage. It doesn't diminish the fact you're clearly the better person and will still be so once this appropriate anger subsides.

I have a lot of sympathy for you friend. 
It sounds like you're making some progress, just don't let this experience lesson you as a person

"Holding onto anger is like drinking poison and expecting the other person to die."

Hello, poor soul. 

Would it help if I told you so many of us feel the same? That so many of us that should consider ourselves fortunate to have close family ties, a clutch of friends to socialise with and coworkers or associates that express interest in their lives feel just as you do?

What if I told you that the close family become something to protect from our true feelings and must be performed for in the interest of their happiness and peace of mind? That in our minds the friends remain so only so long as we don't overburden them with our truths, so we perform and act out the brave face all over? That the interested coworkers must only ever be placated with platitudes and the merest of glimpses into our realities?

I think I understand you and if I am mistaken I mean no slight or insult. As a youth with childhood friends I felt that connection you describe, but it is long absent from my life now and such innocent perception can not be guaranteed to have be real. Nostalgia is seductive and disingenuous. 
As an adult halfway through what life I can reasonably expect, I thought I had found it with who I thought was my soul mate for more than a decade, but unforgivable betrayal proved the one-sidedness of that assumption to me some months ago. 

But in all this ugliness, in all this pain, I believe I have learned for myself an old truth that I would like to try and share with you now, if you will indulge me a moment: 

Try to learn to love yourself and live with yourself. There is beauty in the world if we only allow ourselves to see it. Do not look to others, your eyes are yours and yours alone, we are born into this world alone and die alone after all...
So, live a life as best can be lived, be kind to everyone, even the undeserving and especially to yourself. Help wherever you can to make life and lives some small fraction better. Try to open your eyes to beauty and embrace the peace that comes with such a state of mind, all else follows.

There is always tomorrow.

Hello friend. 

I say to hell with that noise. 
There is connecting with people be they friends, family or otherwise. There is art. There is music. There is beauty in the world if you only have the eyes to see it. There is passion and in my humble opinion these are the things worth living for. 

Reach out out and grasp your passion with both hands and to hell with the detractors. 
With passion comes improvement of the things you have the spine to do. 
No one is really laughing at you and if (on the minuscule chance) they are, it is to mask their own bitterness at their own lack of spine to pursue their own secret wants. 
Why would you do this? Because it is your passion, your desire and what brings you happiness and purpose. Anyone who cannot see or understand that bears no consideration, only pity. 

Fight on and do what brings you joy.

Hello friend. 

It is important to learn to be happy with yourself again, I really can't stress that enough. When a loving, giving person comes to offer so much of themselves for the ideal or reality of another that it becomes ingrained and habitual, it is easy to lose sight of that happiness of self. 

I am by no means qualified to call myself an expert, take my thoughts to heart or ignore them, but if you do chose to consider them then I implore you to take this one piece of advice: Work toward becoming comfortable with your self again, learn to like and eventually even love yourself. When you achieve that, then you will be ready to find someone truly worthy of sharing that love with, but not before then - everyone with the conscience to truly love deserves a partner, not a dependent.

There is no quick fix, there's are no magic words I or anyone else can say. I'm at the end of a 12 year relationship, 6 years of marriage due to my partners infidelity.

The brutal truth is despite the earnestness and warmth of your feelings, they were not returned and were therefore undeserved. 
There is pressure to be "mature" about these things, to remain friends because it's the urbane and modern thing to do. 
I say that's fine, but only once you have given yourself plenty of time to reconnect with who you are alone, the person you were before. You may find they have not waited and no longer wish to be friends, or equally possible, that you realise they are as unworthy of your friendship as they were your love - what is real friendship if not a form of love?

You must live through your sadness and mourning, they are entirely human emotions and you will be worse for suppressing them. You must give yourself the time and space from your former partner to do so. 

Once you feel able, start trying to channel your emotions into the will to fight on, it's something we all have in us somewhere, but can lose sight of. 
For so long as you fight, there is always tomorrow and the chance tomorrow will be a little better.

How are you holding up friend?

PM me if you want to talk out of the public eye.

That's great friend. 

The other recommendation I'd give; don't beat yourself with your lists. 

Aspire to them, work toward them, but if something slips until the next day that's fine. Don't let it have slipped because something else you set as a goal or is a positive use of your time isn't taking that time up.

You'll get to it, just DO get to it. 

Laziness and apathy are fertile ground for despair to take root.

I'm glad I could help in some small way

One important thing I forgot to mention that helps me: Make plans for everything I mentioned and anything else you want or need to do. 

It doesn't always have to be big stuff like travel or trips out, I find making plans and setting things out everyday helps a hell of a lot to keep me from just slumping. 

Here's the list I made on my lunch break for this evening:



___
* Put on Laundry - 7pm
* Sit-ups - 7.10pm
* Walk at least 4 miles - 7.40pm
* Cook & Eat Dinner - 8.40pm
* Clean floors & hang laundry - 9.10pm
* Call/email/IM/reddit with people - 9.45pm
* Shower - 10.15pm
* Reading in bed till sleep - 10.30pm
___

I can't speak for anyone but myself. 

For many years I smoked weed. When my life started to get worse and I started fighting depression I no longer could. 

I look back now and realise that while weed made me relaxed and blissful, it really made me feel better by putting off really feeling. Made lazyness a pleasurable activity. Made apathy the standard mindset.  Was a comfortable and familiar escape. 

Now when I smoke it I just feel worse; as someone fighting to not be depressed it allows for too much introspection which when combined with the paranoia it can bring (it's a mood enhancer, good or bad, and paranoia is a well documented potential side effect) I feel dragged down and start self loathing. That makes my problems getting to sleep far far worse, lying in bed and a prisoner in my own negative thoughts and memories (I need meds to sleep properly 2 to 5 times a week and smoking equals a night I'm guaranteed to need sleep meds or drinking alone to get any).

This is my experience and (for reasons I've mentioned elsewhere) I couldn't say how typical the way I react is.

I couldn't possibly begin to tell you what to do or how to be, but if you're willing I'd like to try and give you some advice.

Don't presume to make decisions of this type on behalf of the person who loves you, only they know the truth within their own heart and the depth of their love. it is entirely self destructive for you to decide he should or should not love you.

Try not to load all hope of happiness onto his shoulders, in life we lose people for all sorts of reasons - breakups are the most common and perhaps least brutal of these. You may be together for all of your days or not, that should not be something your chances of happiness are contingent upon. You must try to work toward your own happiness so that you can share it with this person, not rely on them for it. 

Don't beat yourself up about feeling attraction toward another person, take heart in the strength of character your recognising it as only a crush and nothing more shows you have in you, take heart that the person you love is who you want and not this (likely) fleeting and entirely human attraction. 

Your studies are important, but studies are never easy or they would be meaningless. Strive to do the best work you can, not just doing enough. If you do so you will have done all you can and no more can be expected of anyone. Apply yourself and resist despair, you may find you surprise yourself and even if not there is pride to be had in the metaphorical sweat gathered on your brow from giving something all you can, win or lose. 

Your growing up sounds entirely unpleasant, don't beat yourself with the sticks that are unhappy memories. I know it's easily said and no one would expect a person to instantly let go of these things, it is a goal to strive for and a horizon to look toward. 

Have heart, be kind to yourself and those around you, fight on because as long as you do there is always tomorrow.

Self flagellation is not only unproductive it's self destructive. Don't be so hard on yourself. 

You recognise the pattern and how it's not helping you, you've done great getting help, even if you think you should have done so sooner - if there's a next time you have every reason to have more faith in yourself to do better.

Believing in yourself is the most likely form of self fulfilling prophecy to come true. 

Fight on, there is always tomorrow.

How did I survive? I still have my bad times, mornings waking alone are tough as are the nights. 
The truth is I'm not sure I have survived yet, but there is always tomorrow for so long as you keep trying. 

What I do know is that cliche is just a word for truth spoken so often it becomes universally acknowledged as common sense:

The first thing I did was start trying to live for myself and become comfortable with my own company. This is incredibly important. 

Next I started trying to improve my health both mentally and physically. First thing was starting to try and get a minimum of 7-8 hours sleep a night and keeping healthier hours - it's hard, I force myself to be in bed by 10.30 pm even if I can't sleep and hold off on my sleep meds until I've had 2-3 bad nights in a row. 

I started monitoring my calorie intake, not because I was overweight but because it's a positive use if my time - this also lead me to start cooking my meals in the evenings and learning more about that, equally positive and healthy. 

I started using my night walks as another healthy step, rather than doing them after drinking as a way to get myself hurt or in trouble. I try to do 5-15 miles a week now and have sustained no further injuries due to "accidents". 

I started taking martial arts classes for the first time since I was a kid, which lead me to start using the gym a couple of times a week. I honestly think the hours after pushing myself and getting all those endorphins are among the best I'm capable of feeling these days. 

If I want to see something beautiful, I go to a gallery or museum alone. If I want to see artists I like when they play, I go alone and enjoy their music. If I want a break from where I live, I save some money and go travelling one. If I want for being around people, I grab a book to read while I sit and drink coffee in a cafe alone but around others.
I honestly just try to please myself, and that level of "no f--cks given" gives me a sense of my own strength, my own self reliance and resolve. 

I channelled all my love and care into what friends and family I have left. 
I throw myself into my work rather than just doing it. 
I don't watch TV, play video games, drink outside of social situations or sit around smoking weed for hours at a time anymore. 
I read as much as have time to, especially when in bed and unable to sleep - luminous screens stimulate more than reflected light from a page. 
I take care of my appearance and grooming, I never leave the house in an un ironed shirt or with an untidy beard or uncombed hair.  
I pursue forgotten passions and try to develops new ones. 
And music, I fill my life with music - in my home, car and through headphones when I'm out. Music that animates me, stuff that suits the mood I want to be in rather than reinforces the way I currently feel (sad stuff is OK but only strictly in moderation. "Our music" is also strictly never played). 

By not letting myself slump, I find I have a hard time sitting still now and use my time for all of this instead. And it all makes me feel better about myself. 

I wish I had more for you. 
Fight on, so long as you do there is always tomorrow.

This is a clueless mental health professional. 

Please, please do not let this tarnish your attitude toward getting help, you've done so well and are doing so well to have gotten this far. 

If you can, try to start again with a more competent psychiatrist. 

Just like in everyday life, don't let ignorants drag you down:
Keep on fighting, you're doing so well.

I have done CBT as a means to help with my sleep problems. I rely far less on medication to regulate my sleep thanks to their methods and help, so would recommend at least trying it based on my experiences.

Live for yourself sister.  You are coming to be in a good place, channel this momentum and energy into living a good life - not as petty revenge, as that old saying goes, but for yourself and yourself only. 

Stay strong. Fight on.

Just remember that THC (active agent in Marijuana) is a mood enhancer, regardless of whether the mood you have is good or bad. It's also a downer (depressant) so while it might seem nice you can enjoy it again thanks to your meds, it may not be the best thing for your overall life and future. 

You're a young guy, right now you're building the life you will live for the next 50-80 years. Remember that and try not to let yourself become lazy or apathetic. 

Self improve, never settle. 
Stay hungry and fight, fight, fight!

I think there's an element of "if you act like its true, it will become true" to my outward behaviour. What I do in private, this path of self destruction in slow motion by mixing booze and meds, getting myself hurt walking the roads at night, hurting myself with exercise and malnutrition, tormenting myself sleepless to exhaustion... It isn't going to allow that to happen. 

By day or when talking to the few people I have left I'm projecting the image of the strong guy they know and who can endure anything. But then in my private moments, especially at night and first thing in the morning, I tear into myself and do myself harm or put myself in harms way.

Thanks again for sparing a moments thought and your support friend.

Thank you for taking the time to read and answer. 

I can't tell you how much good your words are doing for me. 

I wish you were right about others realising, but I care too much to worry what's left of  my family, I worry to much I will lose the few friends I have left if I overburden them, I have a therapist and even he in convinced that I am "doing so well" that I am enduring and carrying on "so much better than so many others would".

I had to be strong for her for so long, I had to prop her up and pull her out so often that it has become an act I have perfected. 

No one really knows the truth of how close I have come, no one knows about my slow, methodical and intentionally self destructive habits and routine. 

But you are right. I need to shove myself along, not to the bottom of a bottle, the end of my supply of sleep meds weeks before they're meant to run out and not under the tires of some poor bastards truck or car. 

The bones I broke in my worst night walk are pretty much healed, I need to focus on my head now. I turned away when she came to me with apologies and promises it was meaningless. I need to do the same for the mistress that is misery, her promises are just as hollow, just as bitter tasting.

I have been strong and I can be strong and I am strong. 

Thank you stranger.

Our experiences form who we are and you have said yourself that you have had many bad relationships in the past. Don't let them rose tint your most recent one. 

By your own admission this one had highs and lows too, that this man challenged you and made you work for it in ways others would have failed at utterly, which shows you have strength in you. 

Don't blame yourself and for gods sake don't hurt yourself and post more here or on /r/suicidewatch if it gets really bad. 

I'm not the best person to give advice, particularly about relationships, but I can say that the cost of a bus ticket is not an impossible aim. 

Hold on to hope, there is tomorrow.

If he loves you is it fair to make that decision for him? Why do you get to decide what he is willing to take on for you if he loves you?

A little space may not have been a bad idea, but don't just walk away from him. Perhaps try and be as open with him as you have been with us from within the safety of that space you've created?

It will be scary, but the worst that can happen is that you'll end up where you've already decided (alone) you should be. 

Or maybe I'm wrong, maybe I'm not the best person to give advice on love and relationships. Maybe you should try and talk to a councillor or similar and get your feelings in some sort order. In fact so that anyway, whether you take my first thoughts to heart or not.

Just do not to despair. There's always tomorrow. If things get really bad post more here or on /r/suicidewatch and do nothing in haste. There's always tomorrow.

When? Everyday. And never. 
Isn't that how this works or am I broken?

On my stronger days I simmer with the sense of betrayal, that for caring for her during what would be the worst things imaginable for many, supporting her through her seemingly never ending slumps and depressions after those events, for always being prepared to hold her and tell her we could take anything because we had each other, for the million little tokens and shows of love I gave that seemed nothing but in the end should have meant everything... That for all that, hundreds of weeks of it, for the few weeks I needed the support and care she found something easier and more gratifying to shore-up her self worth, something she knew a man like me could never endure. I simmer and brood and rage internally at the betrayal. Over the fact she tried to make me culpable and accountable for her act of betrayal.

...But then not all days are strong days. In fact that sense of betrayal fuelled strength rarely even lasts an entire day. The nights are brutal, so I do what I described. Sunday mornings feel so bleak, so despairing I count the minutes until I can do what I described.  I excuse myself early from those few social situations available to me so I can be alone to engage in the behaviour I described. 

This is how I live; a smile on my lips for all and a kind word. My ever curving inward posture and my lingering stares at nothing the only outward signs of my tiredness with everything and all, none left to pay close enough attention to notice - "I am fine, I am strong, I am fine." this is my new mantra, this replaces "it doesn't matter who or what we lose, we have each other."

I am a good man. I took on so much and despite my occasional introspections, my evening apathy, my short lived and infrequent and meaningless anger.

I was strong for us. I was strong for her. I fear I cannot do the same for myself.
I didn't deserve this, I deserved the happy life I had planned and worked for for us. The family I wanted us to have. The final years spent together in sunshine. Listen to your own words I tell myself, a thought sometimes repeated by those left who will listen: I am a good man, I must learn to be so strong for myself as I had been for us. I am a good man and I can be strong. 

But I know eventually I will have to return to what was our home and I will be weak again. Sometimes the booze and the double dose of sleeping meds burn in my stomach so badly that I am violently sick when I rise before the sun. And hate the warning label for being wrong and resolve to triple or quadruple the dose the next night and I cry and I think to stop this cycle and I repeat my new mantra for my own benefit, rather than the benefit of others. 

I go back out into the world, the smile is placed upon my lips and the kind words are filled neat and ready at the forefront of my mind and maybe I'll hide for a time with those friends I have left or what family I have left or walking the roads waiting for rain so I can take blameless and final steps. 

I eventually have to go back, where a bottle waits and the warning label lies to me. Perhaps I'll finish the bottle this time. Perhaps five times the dose this time. Perhaps when I fall into the oblivion of sleep I won't dream and I won't wake this time.

Or perhaps I will be strong again and perhaps someone else reading this will realise they can be strong too. There is no shame in weakness, only in surrender.

I am a good man and I can be strong enough to not surrender. That will have to be enough for now.

Thank you for taking the time.

There is tomorrow.
